programme: A hypoxia/oxidative-stress-induced transcriptional-epigenetic reprogramming axis: CREBBP acetylates and coactivates stress-responsive transcription factors, YBX1 couples this to NF-κB-driven metabolic reprogramming and, in ferroptosis-linked injury, to translational stress control, and ETV5 supplies a countervailing Nrf2-dependent antioxidant arm that limits the damage the CREBBP/YBX1 axis responds to.
role_in_a: In papillary/renal carcinoma, this axis is documented as driving LDHA-linked glycolytic reprogramming and NF-κB activation (YBX1), contributing to prognostic methylation and immune-infiltration signatures (YBX1), and appearing among genomically altered loci in an RCC cohort (CREBBP) — consistent with epigenetic and metabolic tumor-supportive functions.
role_in_b: In ischemic stroke, the same nodes are documented in post-ischemic microglial neuroinflammation and YBX1-GPX4 ferroptosis cascades, in altered histone-acetylation biomarker signatures (CREBBP), and in an Nrf2/HACE1-dependent antioxidant response that restrains microglial M1 polarization (ETV5) — i.e. a stress-injury/inflammation arm and an injury-limiting antioxidant arm operating in the same tissue.
shared_axis: Both a solid tumor under metabolic/genotoxic stress and post-ischemic tissue under hypoxic/oxidative stress activate the same CREBBP-acetylation/YBX1-NF-κB stress-response layer, with ETV5-Nrf2 signaling acting as a shared brake on the resulting inflammatory and ferroptotic damage; clinically, malignancy (including renal cancers) is a recognized, if secondary, driver of paraneoplastic hypercoagulability and stroke risk, giving a plausible route by which the two conditions could engage overlapping stress programs.
reasoning: CREBBP and YBX1 each have independent, disease-specific literature and/or high Open Targets percentiles in both diseases, and ETV5 has a strong kidney Open Targets percentile (0.91) plus a direct stroke mechanistic paper, so the module is nameable and partly grounded rather than invented. But no retrieved source connects papillary RCC and stroke through this axis directly — the cross-disease link rests on reasoning (shared stress-response biology, general cancer-stroke comorbidity) rather than on anything retrieved, and the stroke arm here is built from blood, not brain, tissue.
support: 41507134 — YBX1 drives LDHA-mediated metabolic reprogramming and NF-κB activation in kidney/renal cancer; 37523897 — YBX1-linked 5-methylcytosine prognostic signature in kidney renal carcinoma; 34858833 — YBX1-associated CD8+ T-cell infiltration signature in kidney renal carcinoma; 42665256 — microglial RIOK3 phosphorylates YBX1, promoting post-ischemic neuroinflammation; 42304629 — YBX1-GPX4 ferroptosis cascade shown active in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury; 37427096 — CREBBP among genomic alterations in a renal cell carcinoma cohort; 42004604 — CREBBP flagged as a histone-acetylation-linked candidate biomarker in ischemic stroke; 40562126 — ETV5 improves ischemic stroke via HACE1/Nrf2 axis, inhibiting microglial M1 polarization.
how_to_falsify: Inhibit CBP/p300 acetyltransferase activity (e.g. A-485) in a papillary RCC line and in an oxygen-glucose-deprivation model of PBMCs/microglia matched to the blood-derived network used here; the shared-axis prediction is that this blunts YBX1-dependent NF-κB target induction (e.g. glycolytic/TNF genes) and blunts ETV5/Nrf2 antioxidant gene induction in both systems. If CBP/p300 inhibition changes YBX1 or ETV5 output in only one system, or in neither, the shared axis does not hold.
caveats: The stroke arm of this pair is built from blood, not brain, tissue, so the microglial/ferroptosis mechanisms in the cited stroke papers should be read as evidence for these factors' stress biology in ischemic injury generally, not as proof the blood-derived network reflects brain-specific action. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 42 patient-group comparisons, so the appearance of broad replication may partly reflect subgroup redundancy within a small number of cohorts rather than independent confirmation. The exclusion of canonical immune/interferon factors (IRF1, STAT1, SPI1, IRF8, VDR, SPIB, BCL3, CREB5, PRDM1, STAT5B) as tissue-generic means this account is not simply re-describing generic blood/kidney immune-cell composition — but of the 12 surviving factors, only CREBBP, YBX1 and ETV5 have literature or strong Open Targets placement; ZNF16, HOXB7, ISL1, AEBP1, RFX3, ST18, NSD2, NR2F2 and ID1 currently lack support for either disease and were left out of the programme rather than forced in.
